p166.s3.b5: The narrator calls this a truly new and strange interpretation of the old proverb about the straight and narrow way. The apostles were slowly grasping the meaning of the early declaration that one must be born again, yet they still did not fully understand the teaching that spiritual power must be used to overcome the world’s obstacles. The door stands open, but walking through it takes will and spiritual decision.
p166.s4.h: IV. Teaching about Accidents — Health Is Not the Smile of Heaven
p166.s4.b0: At lunch on the way to Philadelphia, Thomas asked whether spirit beings take part in strange events of the material world, and whether angels can prevent accidents. Jesus asked whether he had not noticed that he had consistently refused to use heavenly powers for his personal sustenance. Then he declared it a superstition to regard prosperity as a sign of divine approval and adversity as a sign of God’s displeasure.
p166.s4.b1: He pointed to the Galileans killed by Pilate and the eighteen killed when the tower of Siloam fell. They were not greater sinners than others; they were innocent victims of the accidents of time. Then he divided the events of life into three kinds.

head: Kind of event
The text’s explanation
rows: 1. Ordinary happenings
Part of living on earth with one’s fellows
2. Accidents of nature and human misfortunes
Not prearranged or brought about by spiritual forces
3. The results of effort that follows natural law
Follow the laws of fruitfulness and you reap a harvest — the parable of the fig tree

p166.s4.b4: To illustrate the third kind, Jesus told the parable of the fig tree. A tree that had borne no fruit for three seasons was about to be cut down, but the gardener asked for one more year to dig around it and fertilize it. When they followed the laws of fruitfulness, the tree yielded an abundant harvest. The result came not from a miracle but from work that respected the law.
p166.s4.b5: The Father bestows material things without discrimination, but spiritual gifts are limited only by the capacity of the one receiving them — by faith and by willingness to abide by the Father’s will. The apostles did not fully grasp this teaching. The text remarks that one hour of teaching cannot wholly change the beliefs of a lifetime, which is why Jesus repeated these things many times.
p166.s4.b7: This teaching gives a twofold comfort to those who suffer. It frees them from the guilt of thinking misfortune is God’s punishment, and it restores the value of faithful effort that respects natural law. God’s care shows itself less in preventing accidents than in giving spiritual gifts to the human soul.
p166.s5.h: V. The Congregation at Philadelphia — Abner’s Solitary Faithfulness
p166.s5.b0: Of all the cities of Perea, Philadelphia saw the largest number enter the kingdom. Its synagogue had never been under the supervision of the Sanhedrin and so was never closed, and Abner taught there three times a day. This synagogue later became a church, the headquarters for missions to the east, and for centuries remained a center of Christian learning.
p166.s5.b1: After Jesus’ death the church at Philadelphia came into serious conflict with the Jerusalem church under James. The text explains that because of this discord, the gospel records preserve nothing about Abner and his work. Abner broke with Peter and James over administrative questions and with Paul over differences of philosophy and theology.

head: With whom he broke
Why
rows: Peter and James
Administrative questions and the jurisdiction of the Jerusalem church
Paul
Differences of philosophy and theology — he rejected attempts to remake Jesus’ teachings
What he nonetheless supported

p166.s5.b3: He lived an isolated life, yet during his later years and for some time after, the believers at Philadelphia held more strictly than any other group on earth to the religion of Jesus as he lived and taught it. Abner remained a faithful believer in and teacher of the gospel of the kingdom until he died in A.D. 74 at the age of eighty-nine.
p166.s6.b0: What runs through Paper 166 is the distinction between appearance and reality. Washing the hands is not purity of soul, descent is no qualification for salvation, prosperity is not God’s approval, and illness is not God’s frown. Jesus stripped away these illusions one by one and led people to the realities of faith, gratitude, and devotion to the Father’s will.
